summary.title: Video-MME-v2: Towards the Next Stage in Benchmarks for Comprehensive Video Understanding

details: Existing video-understanding benchmarks are saturating and per-question accuracy inflates scores, hiding whether models comprehend videos robustly and faithfully rather than guessing.

Video-MME-v2: a human-annotated video QA benchmark (800 videos, 3,200 questions, 8 options each) organized into a progressive tri-level capability hierarchy: visual information aggregation -> temporal dynamics -> complex reasoning.

Questions are structured as 4-question groups of two kinds: consistency groups (same capability probed across aspects/granularities) and coherence groups (a staged reasoning chain toward one complex conclusion).

Group-based non-linear scoring instead of per-question accuracy: consistency groups score (N/4)^2 to suppress isolated lucky hits, coherence groups use first-error truncation so only the leading unbroken chain of correct reasoning steps earns credit.
800 web videos, average 10.4 minutes (99% under 20 min), across 4 top-level domains and 31 subcategories (sports, lifestyle, art, knowledge/education).
Recency-oriented anti-contamination: >80% published in 2025 or later, ~40% after October 2025; manual exclusion of classic films/TV and flagship influencer content.
View-count thresholding as quality proxy (84.3% above 10k views).
Taxonomy of 12 sub-categories and 30+ leaf task types with annotation-guideline definitions.
12 annotators, 50 independent reviewers, ~3,300 human-hours, up to 5 rounds of quality assurance; each sample reviewed by at least 2 QC staff.
Text-only Gemini-3-Pro baseline used to remove language-shortcut-solvable questions; adversarial stress-testing with frontier models during annotation.
8 options per question (12.5% chance level), length-controlled options, at least one adversarial distractor per question.
Reviewers answered all questions themselves to establish the human-expert baseline.
Two input settings: visual frames only (wo sub) and frames + subtitles/ASR, or raw audio for omni models (w. sub).
Metrics: per-question Avg Acc, group non-linear score, plus per-level (L1-L3) and per-group-type (consistency/coherence) breakdowns.

Frame budgets follow each model's capability: 64 or 512 frames for open-source models, native rates (e.g., 1fps) for commercial APIs; GPT-5 at 50 frames, Gemini via compressed frames due to API limits.
Commercial: Gemini-3-Pro/Flash, GPT-5, Doubao-Seed-2.0-Pro, MiMo-v2-Omni, Kimi-K2.5.
Open-source instruct and thinking variants: Qwen3.5 (4B-397B, incl. Omni), Qwen3-VL, Qwen2.5-VL, InternVL3.5, GLM-4.1V/4.5V/4.6, KimiVL, MiMo-VL, LLaVA-Video, VideoLLaMA3, VITA-1.5, Keye-VL.
Ablations/analyses: thinking vs instruct mode, 64 vs 512 frames, capability profiling (omni-modal aggregation / long-context / reasoning), Non-Lin/Avg-Acc robustness ratio.

key_findings.finding: Video-MME-v2 is far from saturated, with a large gap between the best model and human experts.
key_findings.evidence: Human experts reach a non-linear score of 90.7 (94.9% avg accuracy) versus 49.4 for Gemini-3-Pro, 43.3 for Doubao-Seed-2.0-Pro, and 39.1 for the best open-source model Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-Think; the weakest tested models fall below 10.

key_findings.finding: Group-based non-linear scoring reveals inconsistency that per-question accuracy hides, and the Non-Lin/Avg-Acc ratio separates robust from fragile models.
key_findings.evidence: Gemini-3-Pro drops from 66.1 avg accuracy to 49.4 non-linear (ratio 74.7%) and Doubao from 60.5 to 43.3 (71.6%), while LLaVA-Video-7B drops from 24.0 to 9.7 (40.4%); consistency groups show flat Q1-Q4 accuracy whereas coherence groups decline monotonically.

key_findings.finding: Performance degrades monotonically across the three hierarchy levels, indicating errors in perception and temporal modeling propagate into a bottleneck for high-level reasoning.
key_findings.evidence: All evaluated models score highest on Level 1 and lowest on Level 3 (e.g., Gemini-3-Pro 64.0 / 50.0 / 40.6 with subtitles); radar analysis shows Action & Motion and Physical World Reasoning below 30 even for SOTA.

key_findings.finding: Thinking modes help when textual cues are available but can hurt in purely visual settings, exposing over-reliance on language priors.
key_findings.evidence: Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-Think gains +3.8 (wo sub) vs +5.8 (w. sub) over its instruct counterpart, whereas Qwen3-VL-8B loses 0.6 without subtitles and KimiVL-16B degrades by 3.3/3.3 overall and 4.0/3.9 at Level 3.

key_findings.finding: Native audio input and long-context frame budgets both yield large gains, and open-source models are more fragile to removing text/audio side information than commercial ones.
key_findings.evidence: With raw audio, Gemini-3-Pro improves 38.2 to 49.4 (+11.2) and MiMo-v2-Omni 29.9 to 38.6 (+8.7); Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-Think rises from 30.6 at 64 frames to 39.1 at 512 frames; commercial models under wo sub (e.g., Doubao 35.2, GPT-5 26.4) exceed the best open-source instruct model with subtitles (25.0).
